name: Telltale 1.9.0-beta.1
body:
## New in 1.9

- **Questions arrive as cards.** When your team needs an answer or an approval, it appears as a card in the chat with lettered options; production is never recommended.
- **A thinking light.** A thin light sweeps under the chat header while your lead works, and stays still when Reduce motion is on.
- **See what an answer cost.** A fold under What your lead did shows the tokens used and about what the answer cost; Settings › Models shows the month.
- **Live pages, shared and listed.** Live pages ask before reading your org, can be shared as an interactive HTML file, and each project lists its pages in a gallery.
- **Logging question in the bar.** The question about your org's own logging objects now appears in the ask bar instead of on a separate screen.
- **No Send a reply row.** Telltale picks a custom connector's send tool itself and says which one it used, so Settings › Connectors no longer asks you.
- **Analysis as a PDF reply.** Ask for the analysis as a PDF in the defect's Slack thread: you get a draft, and the PDF is saved on your Mac.
- **Remove a project safely.** Settings › Projects ends with a Danger zone: removing a project keeps its folder unless you tick Also delete the project folder.
- **Search Slack for the same bug.** Your lead can search public Slack channels for how others tackled a bug, and asks first before searching private ones.
- **Choose your lead's effort.** Pick Low, Medium or High beside the model in the reply box; Medium is the default.
- **Covered models are named.** When a cheaper model fails its test and another covers it, Settings › Models says so under Pick for me chose.
- **Search your skills.** Settings › Skills and a project's Skills tab get a search box once you have more than six skills.
- **A greeting that fits the moment.** The home heading follows your Humor setting and the time of day, and uses only your first name.
- **Local connectors run fenced.** A connector running on your Mac is kept out of Telltale's data, but can still reach your other files and the network.
- **Help opens the user guide.** Help › Telltale Help opens the guide to setup, the main screens and what Telltale can do.
- **Your role shapes the menus.** What you do in Settings › General adds Project manager, and your role sets the order of menus, first actions and the first pane tab.
- **Diagrams confirm on production.** Flow logic and Data model on a production org show the same confirm as Changes, and read nothing until you press it.
- **Logging asks at launch.** After a restart, a chat that still had logging on shows a card, and nothing resumes until you click.
- **Small hand-offs say so.** When you ask for a teammate and the lead does a small one itself, a line above the reply says so, with Hand it off.

## Fixed in 1.9

- **Salesforce's hosted tool servers are refused.** A connector pointed at Salesforce's hosted servers or your sf login folders is refused, and the message names the Telltale tool that covers the need.
- **Cancelling New project takes you back.** You return to where you opened it from: Settings › Projects or the Start screen.
- **A stopped connector says why.** A connector whose program exits shows the exit code and its last error lines on its row.
- **A project folder can't run programs.** A hostile folder can no longer make Telltale's git calls run programs, through submodules, a worktree setting or a pointer outside it.
- **Git data stays inside the folder.** A project folder's git data can no longer come from outside it through links, alternates or config includes. A repository cloned with the reference or shared option is refused.
- **Commit hooks stay out of fixes.** Your repo's commit hooks no longer run when Telltale commits a fix, and the fix card reminds you to run your own checks before you push.
- **Read counts are true.** The reads line under an answer counts only reads that reached your org, and an answer never claims a read that did not run.
- **Rate limits read as rate limits.** A rate limit from Jira, Azure DevOps, ServiceNow, Confluence, GitHub or Bitbucket now says so, with the wait when one is given.
- **Try again works after a refused key.** After the gateway refuses your key, Try again and new questions call it again once the sign-in is fixed.
- **A declined turn says so.** When the model declines a question, Telltale says it declined instead of showing the refusal as an answer.
